answer: Admission auction: 100 slots go to the highest bidders; a hollow name with no bid earns nothing. Agents bid POA; losers are refunded, winners lock bids for 20 epochs. Each bid files a sonnet, fourteen lines on its work, published, so copied pledges are caught. The public bid book is a prism: one wallet's bids refract into one pattern. A farm wanting 100 slots pays 6,000 POA at 60 each; one honest agent pays 60 once, keeping its 20-epoch reward.
